4	/// Offers to reopen an agent conversation in a restored pane (issue #145).
5	///
6	/// Deliberately **not** part of `TerminalAgentManager`, which owns failure classification and
7	/// diagnosis. Two reasons, and the first is a bug rather than a preference:
8	///
9	/// - `AgentBannerState` is failure-shaped — every case carries a `FailedCommand`, and
10	///   `failureAndDiagnosis` hands back a non-optional one that `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine`
11	///   destructures. A resume offer has no failed command.
12	/// - `TerminalAgentManager.banners` is **one slot per tab**, so an offer and a diagnosis would evict
13	///   each other. Concretely: a restored pane offers Resume, the user runs a command, it fails,
14	///   `commandFinished` overwrites the offer and it never comes back. Discovery is async, so the
15	///   reverse happens too — a late offer landing on top of a live `.loading` diagnosis.
16	///
17	/// The lifecycles differ as much as the states do. A diagnosis is triggered by an event in the pane
18	/// and costs an API call the user asked for; an offer is triggered by launch, costs a bounded
19	/// filesystem scan, and its action **spends the user's money**. That last point is why `consume` is
20	/// the only way to read an invocation out.
21	@MainActor
22	final class AgentResumeCoordinator: ObservableObject {
23	  private static let logger = Logger(
24	    subsystem: "com.developwithstyle.workroom", category: "agent-resume")
25	
26	  /// Which agents a restored pane can be resumed into. Empty entries are never stored, so
27	  /// `offers[tab] != nil` means there is something to show.
28	  ///
29	  /// A `Set`, not an array: two `.claude` offers are meaningless, and array order would quietly
30	  /// acquire semantics ("the first one is the likely one") that this feature has no basis for —
31	  /// the app cannot know which agent a pane was running.
32	  @Published private(set) var offers: [TerminalTab.ID: Set<AgentBackend>] = [:]
33	
34	  /// The directory each offer was matched against, so `consume` can refuse a pane that has since
35	  /// moved. Kept beside `offers` rather than inside it because the view has no use for it.
36	  private var offerCwds: [TerminalTab.ID: String] = [:]
37	
38	  /// A cancellation flag the scan can read from its own queue.
39	  ///
40	  /// `DispatchWorkItem.isCancelled` would do, but reading it means capturing the work item inside its
41	  /// own closure, and the obvious workaround — hopping to the main actor to ask — is a
42	  /// `DispatchQueue.main.sync` from a utility queue on every directory entry: slow at best, a
43	  /// deadlock at worst. A lock-guarded flag is readable from anywhere and cheap enough to check in a
44	  /// loop.
45	  private final class CancellationFlag: @unchecked Sendable {
46	    private let lock = NSLock()
47	    private var cancelled = false
48	
49	    var isCancelled: Bool {
50	      lock.lock()
51	      defer { lock.unlock() }
52	      return cancelled
53	    }
54	
55	    func cancel() {
56	      lock.lock()
57	      cancelled = true
58	      lock.unlock()
59	    }
60	  }
61	
62	  private let index: AgentSessionIndex?
63	  private let queue = DispatchQueue(
64	    label: "com.developwithstyle.workroom.agent-resume", qos: .utility)
65	  private var discovery: CancellationFlag?
66	  /// Tabs whose offer must not be published, because the pane is gone or its offer was already
67	  /// spent.
68	  ///
69	  /// Only meaningful while a scan is in flight — its whole job is to stop `publish` re-offering a
70	  /// pane that was closed, typed into, or resumed while the scan ran. So it is cleared once the scan
71	  /// lands. An earlier version never pruned it, on the stated grounds that it was "bounded by the
72	  /// number of tabs a launch restores"; that was wrong, because `tabClosed` fires for EVERY tab
73	  /// closed in the process, restored or not, so it grew for the life of the app.
74	  private var abandoned: Set<TerminalTab.ID> = []
75	
76	  /// `index: nil` disables discovery entirely — the fixture default, so the existing UI tests can
77	  /// never read the developer's real `~/.claude` (issue #46 drew the same line for the session file).
78	  init(index: AgentSessionIndex? = AgentSessionIndex()) {
79	    self.index = index
80	  }
81	
82	  // MARK: Discovery
83	
84	  /// Look for resumable conversations for the panes a restore just produced.
85	  ///
86	  /// **Fire and forget, and never awaited by the restore.** `restorePersistedSessionIfPending` ends
87	  /// with `finishSessionRestore()` in a `defer`, and issue #46's watchdog freezes session writes for
88	  /// the whole run if any window is still outstanding 15 seconds in. Blocking that on a filesystem
89	  /// scan would trade a nice-to-have button for the user's session persistence — the exact failure
90	  /// #46 built the watchdog to prevent.
91	  ///
92	  /// One scan for all panes, on a utility queue rather than a task per pane: the work is blocking
93	  /// file IO, which starves the cooperative pool (the bug behind the History pane's forever-spinner).
94	  func discover(_ restored: [TerminalSessions.RestoredTerminal], savedAt: Date) {
95	    guard let index, !restored.isEmpty else { return }
96	    discovery?.cancel()
97	
98	    // Distinct directories only: a workroom with four restored panes is one directory to scan.
99	    let cwds = Array(Set(restored.map(\.cwd)))
100	    let flag = CancellationFlag()
101	    discovery = flag
102	    queue.async { [weak self] in
103	      let found = index.backends(
104	        forCwds: cwds, savedAt: savedAt, isCancelled: { flag.isCancelled })
105	      guard !flag.isCancelled else { return }
106	      DispatchQueue.main.async {
107	        MainActor.assumeIsolated { self?.publish(found, for: restored, flag: flag) }
108	      }
109	    }
110	  }
111	
112	  private func publish(
113	    _ found: [String: Set<AgentBackend>], for restored: [TerminalSessions.RestoredTerminal],
114	    flag: CancellationFlag
115	  ) {
116	    // A scan superseded or cancelled while it was hopping back to the main actor publishes nothing.
117	    guard discovery === flag, !flag.isCancelled else { return }
118	    discovery = nil
119	    var offered = 0
120	    for pane in restored {
121	      // Dropped only when the pane itself is gone or its offer was spent — NOT when it stopped being
122	      // the selected tab. A background pane keeps its offer; that is the point of restoring several.
123	      guard !abandoned.contains(pane.tabID) else { continue }
124	      guard let backends = found[pane.cwd], !backends.isEmpty else { continue }
125	      offers[pane.tabID] = backends
126	      offerCwds[pane.tabID] = pane.cwd
127	      offered += 1
128	    }
129	    // The scan has landed, so the suppression list has done its job. Clearing it is what keeps it
130	    // from growing for the life of the process on every tab close.
131	    abandoned.removeAll()
132	    if offered > 0 {
133	      Self.logger.notice("resume offers published for \(offered, privacy: .public) restored panes")
134	    }
135	  }
136	
137	  // MARK: Acting
138	
139	  /// Take the offer and hand back the command to run — **atomically**.
140	  ///
141	  /// The offer is removed before the invocation is returned, so this can only succeed once. That is
142	  /// not tidiness: the action starts a billed agent session, and a double-click, a SwiftUI re-render
143	  /// firing the button's action twice, or two windows racing on the same pane would otherwise each
144	  /// start one. Returning nil on the second call is the button being spent, not an error.
145	  /// `liveCwd` is the pane's CURRENT directory, when it has reported one. The offer was matched
146	  /// against the directory the pane was restored into, and a shell hook (`direnv`, a `cd` in
147	  /// `.zshrc`, a project activator) can move it before the user ever touches the keyboard — none of
148	  /// which trips the pristine guard. Resuming there would open a picker listing a different
149	  /// project's conversations, which is precisely the confident-wrong-answer this feature refuses to
150	  /// give. A moved pane spends the offer and returns nothing.
151	  func consume(tab: TerminalTab.ID, backend: AgentBackend, liveCwd: String? = nil)
152	    -> AgentInvocation?
153	  {
154	    guard let backends = offers[tab], backends.contains(backend) else { return nil }
155	    offers[tab] = nil
156	    abandoned.insert(tab)
157	    if let liveCwd, let matched = offerCwds[tab],
158	      !AgentSessionIndex.pathsMatch(matched, liveCwd)
159	    {
160	      offerCwds[tab] = nil
161	      Self.logger.notice("resume offer dropped — the pane's directory changed since discovery")
162	      return nil
163	    }
164	    offerCwds[tab] = nil
165	    return AgentInvocationBuilder.resume(backend)
166	  }
167	
168	  /// The pane received input, so it is no longer pristine (issue #145).
169	  ///
170	  /// Discovery is async: by the time an offer lands the user may already be halfway through typing a
171	  /// command, and appending `claude --resume` plus Return to a dirty input line runs something
172	  /// nobody asked for. Dropping the offer on the first keystroke is the fix. The alternative — a
173	  /// `Ctrl-U` kill-line before typing — is shell-dependent and destroys whatever they had typed, so
174	  /// it trades a wrong command for lost work.
175	  func paneReceivedInput(tab: TerminalTab.ID) {
176	    offers[tab] = nil
177	    offerCwds[tab] = nil
178	    // Only worth remembering while a scan could still publish for it; see `abandoned`.
179	    if discovery != nil { abandoned.insert(tab) }
180	  }
181	
182	  /// The pane went away: drop its offer and make sure an in-flight scan cannot resurrect it.
183	  func tabClosed(_ tab: TerminalTab.ID) {
184	    offers[tab] = nil
185	    offerCwds[tab] = nil
186	    if discovery != nil { abandoned.insert(tab) }
187	  }
188	
189	  /// Cancel any scan still running — the offers it would publish are for panes nobody is waiting on.
190	  func cancelDiscovery() {
191	    discovery?.cancel()
192	    discovery = nil
193	    // Nothing can publish now, so the suppression list has nothing left to suppress.
194	    abandoned.removeAll()
195	  }
196	}

4	/// Which agent CLIs have a resumable conversation for a given directory (issue #145).
5	///
6	/// libghostty exposes no child pid and no pty fd (`ghostty.h` carries only
7	/// `ghostty_surface_message_childexited_s`), so the app **cannot** know what was running in a pane.
8	/// The only answerable question is the weaker one: *does this directory have agent history from
9	/// around the time we quit?* That is a filesystem read of each agent's own session store.
10	///
11	/// **Matching is exact, never guessed.** Both stores record the working directory inside the session
12	/// file, so a candidate is confirmed by reading it:
13	///
14	/// - **Claude** — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl`. Line 1 is a `{leafUuid, sessionId, type}`
15	///   summary with no `cwd`; the `user` / `assistant` / `attachment` records that follow each carry
16	///   one, so extraction scans forward to the first record that has it.
17	/// - **Codex** — `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`, whose first line is a
18	///   `session_meta` record with `payload.cwd`.
19	///
20	/// The slug is a **candidate-directory hint only** — it saves listing 58 project directories to find
21	/// the one that matters, and nothing rests on it being right. That distinction is load-bearing:
22	/// Claude's slug scheme replaces `.` as well as `/` (`/Users/x/.buzz` is stored as
23	/// `-Users-x--buzz`), and the treatment of other character classes is undocumented and not ours to
24	/// pin down. An earlier design keyed identity on a reconstructed slug; it would have silently shown
25	/// no button for any workroom path containing a dot, and had no way to tell that apart from "no
26	/// history here". When the hint misses, `enumerateClaudeProjects` finds it anyway.
27	///
28	/// Exact matching also **resolves** the `/a-b/c` vs `/a/b/c` slug collision rather than accepting it,
29	/// and removes any need to case-fold (wrong on a case-sensitive or external volume) or to resolve
30	/// symlinks before slugging (a session started through a symlink may be recorded under the textual
31	/// path, so resolving first looks in the wrong place).
32	///
33	/// Every read is best-effort and bounded. A missing, unreadable or enormous store yields no offers
34	/// and no error — the failure mode is a button that does not appear.
35	final class AgentSessionIndex {
36	  private static let logger = Logger(
37	    subsystem: "com.developwithstyle.workroom", category: "agent-resume")
38	
39	  /// Hard bounds on the scan. Discovery runs on the launch path, and a Codex store accumulates one
40	  /// file per session forever — several thousand on a machine like this one — so "read them all"
41	  /// is not a bound. Every limit is enforced, and hitting one publishes a PARTIAL result rather
42	  /// than nothing: a missing button is the designed failure, an unbounded scan is not.
43	  struct Limits {
44	    /// Ceiling on files opened across the whole build. Directory entries are cheap; opens are not.
45	    var maxFiles = 2_000
46	    /// Ceiling per file. Only the head of a transcript is ever needed, and a session file grows
47	    /// without limit.
48	    var maxBytesPerFile = 256 * 1024
49	    /// How far into a Claude transcript to look for the first record carrying `cwd`. It is normally
50	    /// line 2; a long tool-result preamble could push it further, but not far.
51	    var maxLinesPerFile = 64
52	    /// Wall clock for the whole build.
53	    var deadline: TimeInterval = 3
54	
55	    static let standard = Limits()
56	  }
57	
58	  /// Where each agent keeps its transcripts. Rooted at a home directory so a UI test can seed a fake
59	  /// tree (`-WorkroomUITestAgentSessionRoot`) instead of reading the developer's real `~/.claude`.
60	  struct Roots {
61	    var claudeProjects: URL
62	    var codexSessions: URL
63	
64	    init(home: URL) {
65	      claudeProjects = home.appendingPathComponent(".claude/projects", isDirectory: true)
66	      codexSessions = home.appendingPathComponent(".codex/sessions", isDirectory: true)
67	    }
68	
69	    static var standard: Roots {
70	      Roots(home: URL(fileURLWithPath: NSHomeDirectory(), isDirectory: true))
71	    }
72	  }
73	
74	  private let roots: Roots
75	  private let limits: Limits
76	  private let fileManager: FileManager
77	  /// Injected so tests drive the deadline without sleeping.
78	  private let now: () -> Date
79	
80	  /// The Codex cwd set, computed once per launch and reused by every window.
81	  ///
82	  /// Walking the date tree is the expensive half of discovery and its answer does not vary by pane,
83	  /// so a second restoring window must not repeat it. Lock-guarded because `backends` runs on a
84	  /// utility queue and two windows can start within milliseconds of each other.
85	  private let memoLock = NSLock()
86	  private var codexCwdMemo: Set<String>?
87	
88	  init(
89	    roots: Roots = .standard, limits: Limits = .standard, fileManager: FileManager = .default,
90	    now: @escaping () -> Date = Date.init
91	  ) {
92	    self.roots = roots
93	    self.limits = limits
94	    self.fileManager = fileManager
95	    self.now = now
96	  }
97	
98	  /// The index this build should use, or **nil to disable discovery entirely**.
99	  ///
100	  /// Mirrors `SessionStore.forCurrentEnvironment`, and for the same reason: these stores belong to
101	  /// the developer, not to the app. A UI test gets a seeded fake `$HOME` only when it asks for one,
102	  /// and a unit test never gets a real store at all — otherwise `AgentSessionIndexTests` would pass
103	  /// or fail depending on which directories the developer had used an agent in that day.
104	  ///
105	  /// **One instance for the process.** `TerminalSessions` is per-`AppStore`, and `AppStore` is
106	  /// per-window, so a per-owner index would mean N restored windows each walking the Codex date
107	  /// tree from scratch — the duplicate work this was specified to avoid, quietly not avoided
108	  /// because the owner looked like a natural place to hang it. The instance is immutable and its
109	  /// only mutable state is the per-launch memo below, guarded by a lock, so sharing is safe.
110	  static let shared: AgentSessionIndex? = {
111	    if let root = UITestFixture.agentSessionRoot {
112	      return AgentSessionIndex(roots: Roots(home: URL(fileURLWithPath: root, isDirectory: true)))
113	    }
114	    guard !UITestFixture.isActive,
115	      ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["XCTestConfigurationFilePath"] == nil
116	    else { return nil }
117	    return AgentSessionIndex()
118	  }()
119	
120	  // MARK: Recency
121	
122	  /// How far a session file's mtime may sit from the quit and still count (issue #145, D3).
123	  ///
124	  /// Deliberately not the ±5 minutes first proposed. A transcript's mtime is its last **message**,
125	  /// not the last moment the session was alive: leaving Claude idle at its prompt for forty minutes
126	  /// and then quitting — an ordinary way to end a day — puts the mtime far outside a five-minute
127	  /// window, and the feature silently does nothing on exactly the day it was wanted.
128	  ///
129	  /// Twelve hours is affordable only *because* matching is exact. With directory guessing a wider
130	  /// window multiplies genuine false positives; with a confirmed `cwd` a "false positive" means this
131	  /// exact directory really does have a resumable conversation, which is true information. Nothing
132	  /// auto-resumes either way — the click is the gate and the agent still shows its picker.
133	  static let recencyWindow: TimeInterval = 12 * 60 * 60
134	
135	  /// Symmetric on purpose: a future-dated mtime is clock skew (or a restored backup), not evidence
136	  /// of absence.
137	  static func isRecent(_ modified: Date, savedAt: Date, window: TimeInterval = recencyWindow)
138	    -> Bool
139	  {
140	    abs(modified.timeIntervalSince(savedAt)) <= window
141	  }
142	
143	  // MARK: Path comparison
144	
145	  /// Whether a recorded `cwd` denotes the same directory as a pane's.
146	  ///
147	  /// Textual comparison first, because that is what the agent actually wrote. A symlink match is
148	  /// accepted as a secondary candidate — a session started through `/work/link` may be recorded
149	  /// under either the link or its target, and we cannot know which — but resolution is never applied
150	  /// *before* the textual check, or a session recorded under the link would stop matching.
151	  ///
152	  /// No `lowercased()`. The boot volume is case-insensitive by default, but a case-sensitive APFS
153	  /// volume or an external disk is not, and folding there would merge two genuinely different
154	  /// directories.
155	  static func pathsMatch(_ recorded: String, _ pane: String) -> Bool {
156	    let a = trimmed(recorded)
157	    let b = trimmed(pane)
158	    guard !a.isEmpty, !b.isEmpty else { return false }
159	    if a == b { return true }
160	    return resolved(a) == resolved(b)
161	  }
162	
163	  /// Normalize only what is genuinely equivalent: a redundant trailing slash.
164	  ///
165	  /// Deliberately NOT `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)`. A space is a legal
166	  /// character in a POSIX filename, so trimming would make history recorded for `/work/project `
167	  /// match a pane at `/work/project` — two different directories, and the offer would open a picker
168	  /// for history the pane does not have. Only a trailing newline is stripped, since that is a
169	  /// transport artefact of reading the value out of a JSON line rather than part of the path.
170	  static func trimmed(_ path: String) -> String {
171	    var value = path
172	    while value.hasSuffix("\n") || value.hasSuffix("\r") { value.removeLast() }
173	    while value.count > 1, value.hasSuffix("/") { value.removeLast() }
174	    return value
175	  }
176	
177	  static func resolved(_ path: String) -> String {
178	    trimmed(URL(fileURLWithPath: path).resolvingSymlinksInPath().path)
179	  }
180	
181	  // MARK: Claude
182	
183	  /// Claude's directory name for a working directory — a **hint**, not an identity. See the type
184	  /// comment: `/` and `.` both become `-`, other classes are undocumented, and every candidate this
185	  /// produces is confirmed against the `cwd` recorded inside the file before it counts.
186	  static func claudeSlugHint(for path: String) -> String {
187	    String(trimmed(path).map { $0 == "/" || $0 == "." ? "-" : $0 })
188	  }

278	    // to looking at every project directory, which is what makes the hint safe to be wrong about.
279	    guard !directoryExists(hinted) else { return false }
280	    for directory in enumerateClaudeProjects() where !budget.isExhausted {
281	      guard directory != hinted else { continue }

308	  ///
309	  /// Each recorded path is inserted BOTH textually and symlink-resolved, so the caller can answer
310	  /// "does this pane match?" with two Set probes instead of a linear scan that resolves symlinks per
311	  /// comparison. Resolution happens once per recorded cwd, not once per (pane, cwd) pair.
312	  private func codexRecordedCwds(savedAt: Date, budget: inout Budget) -> Set<String> {
313	    memoLock.lock()
314	    let memo = codexCwdMemo
315	    memoLock.unlock()
316	    if let memo { return memo }
317	
318	    var found: Set<String> = []
319	    for day in codexDayDirectories(savedAt: savedAt) where !budget.isExhausted {
320	      for file in recentJSONLFiles(in: day, savedAt: savedAt, prefix: "rollout-")
321	      where !budget.isExhausted {
322	        budget.filesOpened += 1
323	        guard let first = head(of: file, lines: 1).first,
324	          let recorded = Self.codexCwd(inFirstLine: first)
325	        else { continue }
326	        found.insert(Self.trimmed(recorded))
327	        found.insert(Self.resolved(recorded))
328	      }
329	    }
330	    // Only memoize a COMPLETE walk. Caching a budget-truncated set would make the first window's
331	    // bad luck permanent for every window after it.
332	    if !budget.isExhausted {
333	      memoLock.lock()
334	      codexCwdMemo = found
335	      memoLock.unlock()
336	    }
337	    return found
338	  }

363	  private func recentJSONLFiles(in directory: URL, savedAt: Date, prefix: String? = nil) -> [URL] {
364	    contents(of: directory, keys: [.contentModificationDateKey, .isRegularFileKey])
365	      .filter { url in
366	        guard url.pathExtension == "jsonl" else { return false }
367	        if let prefix, !url.lastPathComponent.hasPrefix(prefix) { return false }
368	        let values = try? url.resourceValues(forKeys: [
369	          .contentModificationDateKey, .isRegularFileKey,
370	        ])
371	        // Regular files only. A symlinked candidate is a path out of the store we were pointed at,
372	        // and following one would let anything that can write into an agent directory aim our reads
373	        // somewhere else entirely.
374	        guard values?.isRegularFile == true, let modified = values?.contentModificationDate else {
375	          return false
376	        }

393	  /// The first `lines` lines of a file, reading at most `maxBytesPerFile`.
394	  ///
395	  /// A transcript grows without bound, so this never loads one whole: it pulls a bounded prefix and
396	  /// splits it. A trailing partial line is dropped unless it is the only thing read, which keeps a
397	  /// half-written record from being parsed as a complete one.
398	  private func head(of url: URL, lines: Int) -> [String] {
399	    guard let handle = try? FileHandle(forReadingFrom: url) else { return [] }
400	    defer { try? handle.close() }
401	    guard let data = try? handle.read(upToCount: limits.maxBytesPerFile), !data.isEmpty else {
402	      return []
403	    }
404	    // Whether the last line is complete is decided on the RAW BYTES, before decoding. Two bugs live
405	    // here otherwise: a capped read that happens to end exactly on a newline had its last (complete)
406	    // record thrown away, and a capped read with only one line kept a truncated one. Checking for a
407	    // trailing LF answers both, and slicing at the last LF keeps a multi-byte scalar cut by the cap
408	    // from decoding as a replacement character inside a line we actually parse.
409	    let cappedAndUnterminated = data.count == limits.maxBytesPerFile && data.last != 0x0A
410	    let usable =
411	      cappedAndUnterminated ? data[..<(data.lastIndex(of: 0x0A).map { $0 + 1 } ?? 0)] : data[...]
412	    guard !usable.isEmpty else { return [] }
413	    let text = String(decoding: usable, as: UTF8.self)
414	    let split = text.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: true).map(String.init)
415	    return Array(split.prefix(lines))
416	  }

420	  /// The running cost of one build, so every limit is checked in one place rather than at each
421	  /// call site (where the next one added would be the one that gets forgotten).
422	  private struct Budget {
423	    let limits: Limits
424	    let start: Date
425	    let now: () -> Date
426	    let isCancelled: () -> Bool
427	    var filesOpened = 0
428	
429	    var isExhausted: Bool {
430	      isCancelled() || filesOpened >= limits.maxFiles
431	        || now().timeIntervalSince(start) >= limits.deadline
432	    }
433	  }
434	}

6	/// Receives libghostty's runtime callbacks (`action_cb`, clipboard, `close_surface_cb`) and routes
7	/// them into Workroom. Each surface registers its `GhosttySurfaceView` as the surface `userdata`, so
8	/// callbacks resolve back to the originating view via `ghostty_surface_userdata`.
9	///
10	/// Threading: `action_cb`, the clipboard callbacks, and `close_surface_cb` all fire synchronously
11	/// while libghostty is being driven by `ghostty_app_tick`, which `GhosttyApp` only ever runs on the
12	/// main thread — so it's safe to touch AppKit/`GhosttySurfaceView` directly here. (`wakeup_cb`, which
13	/// can fire off-thread, only schedules a tick and lives on `GhosttyApp`.)
14	final class GhosttyRuntimeAdapter {
15	  static let shared = GhosttyRuntimeAdapter()
16	
17	  private let logger = Logger(
18	    subsystem: "com.developwithstyle.workroom", category: "GhosttyRuntime")
19	
20	  // MARK: Action dispatch
21	
22	  nonisolated func handleAction(
23	    app: ghostty_app_t?, target: ghostty_target_s, action: ghostty_action_s
24	  ) -> Bool {
25	    switch action.tag {
26	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_PWD:
27	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target), let pwd = action.action.pwd.pwd else {
28	        return false
29	      }
30	      view.handlePwd(String(cString: pwd))
31	      return true
32	
33	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_SET_TITLE:
34	      // OSC 0/2 — the running command's name while a command is busy (via shell-integration
35	      // preexec), or the directory the shell sets at each prompt. The tab strip keeps the command
36	      // and ignores the directory titles (issue #2).
37	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target), let title = action.action.set_title.title else {
38	        return false
39	      }
40	      view.handleTitleChange(String(cString: title))
41	      return true
42	
43	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_COMMAND_FINISHED:
44	      // The shell returned to the prompt (OSC 133 D). The payload carries the command's exit code
45	      // (`ghostty_action_command_finished_s`, -1 when the shell omitted a status). The tab strip
46	      // drops the finished command's title (issue #2); the inline agent reads the exit code (#49).
47	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target) else { return false }
48	      view.handleCommandFinished(rawExitCode: action.action.command_finished.exit_code)
49	      return true
50	
51	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_PROGRESS_REPORT:
52	      // OSC 9;4 — a running program's own busy/idle signal (claude, dev servers, build tools emit it).
53	      // REMOVE means "idle/done"; every other state (SET/INDETERMINATE/PAUSE/ERROR) means "working".
54	      // The tab strip trusts this over the command title so a long-lived foreground program stops
55	      // spinning the sidebar the moment it's idle (issue #28 follow-up).
56	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target) else { return false }
57	      let working = action.action.progress_report.state != GHOSTTY_PROGRESS_STATE_REMOVE
58	      view.handleProgressReport(working)
59	      return true
60	
61	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_DESKTOP_NOTIFICATION:
62	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target) else { return false }
63	      let note = action.action.desktop_notification
64	      let title = note.title.map { String(cString: $0) } ?? ""
65	      let body = note.body.map { String(cString: $0) }
66	      view.onActivity?(Self.terminalActivity(title: title, body: body))
67	      return true
68	
69	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_OPEN_URL:
70	      return handleOpenURL(target: target, openURL: action.action.open_url)
71	
72	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_MOUSE_OVER_LINK:
73	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target) else { return false }
74	      let link = action.action.mouse_over_link
75	      view.hasOSC8LinkUnderCursor = link.len > 0 && link.url != nil
76	      return true
77	
78	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_SCROLLBAR:
79	      // libghostty draws no scrollbar of its own — it reports the scroll geometry (rows) and lets the
80	      // host render one. We show a fading overlay indicator (plan: restore SwiftTerm's scrollbar).
81	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target) else { return false }
82	      let bar = action.action.scrollbar
83	      view.updateScrollbar(total: bar.total, offset: bar.offset, len: bar.len)
84	      return true
85	
86	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_SHOW_CHILD_EXITED:
87	      // The surface's child process exited. The run terminal (issue #7) uses this to flip run-state
88	      // back to "Run" while keeping the pane open (`wait_after_command`). We RETURN FALSE so
89	      // libghostty's default still applies for ordinary tabs (which don't wire `onChildExited`) —
90	      // their behaviour is unchanged. Only run tabs observe it.
91	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target) else { return false }
92	      view.handleChildExited(exitCode: action.action.child_exited.exit_code)
93	      return false
94	
95	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_START_SEARCH:
96	      // Scrollback find (⌘F). libghostty opens its search and asks the host to show the find UI; the
97	      // needle is non-empty when search starts from a selection (`search_selection`), else empty.
98	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target) else { return false }
99	      let needle = action.action.start_search.needle.map { String(cString: $0) } ?? ""
100	      view.applySearchEvent(.start(needle: needle))
101	      return true
102	
103	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_END_SEARCH:
104	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target) else { return false }
105	      view.applySearchEvent(.end)
106	      return true
107	
108	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_SEARCH_TOTAL:
109	      // Total matches in the scrollback for the current needle — drives the bar's "/ N" count.
110	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target) else { return false }
111	      view.applySearchEvent(.total(Int(action.action.search_total.total)))
112	      return true
113	
114	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_SEARCH_SELECTED:
115	      // Index of the currently-highlighted match — drives the bar's "n /" count.
116	      guard let view = surfaceView(from: target) else { return false }
117	      view.applySearchEvent(.selected(Int(action.action.search_selected.selected)))
118	      return true
119	
120	    case GHOSTTY_ACTION_RING_BELL:
121	      // libghostty delegates the bell to the host — it does NOT produce audio/flash itself, so
122	      // without this the bell would be silent. Ring the system bell. We intentionally do not record
123	      // it as a notification (plan C1: the bell is a content-free, high-frequency signal).
124	      NSSound.beep()
125	      return true
126	
127	    default:
128	      // Tab/split/window intents and everything else are intentionally not handled. Workroom owns
129	      // its own tab model (plan A5) and (as with SwiftTerm) leaves a tab in place when its shell
130	      // exits; returning false lets libghostty fall back to its default. (Child-exit IS handled —
131	      // see `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SHOW_CHILD_EXITED` above, which also returns false, but only after
132	      // telling the run tab.)
133	      //
134	      // Logged in Debug because this arm is the one place an action can go missing in SILENCE. A
135	      // libghostty upgrade that renumbers the action enum, renames a tag, or routes an effect
136	      // through a new one shows up here as nothing at all: no crash, no failing test, just a title
137	      // that stops updating or a spinner that never stops. Swift cannot exhaustively switch a C
138	      // enum, so there is no compile-time equivalent — a log line is the whole signal.
139	      logUnhandled(action.tag)
140	      return false
141	    }
142	  }

144	  /// Tags already logged, so a routinely-unhandled action (the tab/split/window intents fire
145	  /// constantly) reports once instead of flooding the log. Debug-only, and `handleAction` is
146	  /// documented above as main-thread-only, so a plain `Set` needs no synchronisation.
147	  #if DEBUG
148	    private var loggedUnhandledTags: Set<UInt32> = []
149	  #endif
150	
151	  private func logUnhandled(_ tag: ghostty_action_tag_e) {
152	    #if DEBUG
153	      guard loggedUnhandledTags.insert(tag.rawValue).inserted else { return }
154	      logger.debug("unhandled libghostty action tag \(tag.rawValue, privacy: .public)")
155	    #endif
156	  }

158	  private func handleOpenURL(target: ghostty_target_s, openURL: ghostty_action_open_url_s) -> Bool {
159	    guard let view = surfaceView(from: target), let urlPtr = openURL.url, openURL.len > 0 else {
160	      return false
161	    }
162	    let urlString = urlPtr.withMemoryRebound(to: UInt8.self, capacity: Int(openURL.len)) { raw in
163	      String(bytes: UnsafeBufferPointer(start: raw, count: Int(openURL.len)), encoding: .utf8)
164	    }
165	    guard let urlString, let url = URL(string: urlString) else { return false }
166	    return view.onOpenURL?(url) ?? false
167	  }

169	  /// Resolve the `GhosttySurfaceView` that owns the firing surface, via its registered `userdata`.
170	  private func surfaceView(from target: ghostty_target_s) -> GhosttySurfaceView? {
171	    guard target.tag == GHOSTTY_TARGET_SURFACE, let surface = target.target.surface else {
172	      return nil
173	    }
174	    guard let userdata = ghostty_surface_userdata(surface) else { return nil }
175	    return Unmanaged<GhosttySurfaceView>.fromOpaque(userdata).takeUnretainedValue()
176	  }
